findings.title: `sed -i ''` only works with BSD/macOS sed and fails on Linux.
findings.body: GNU sed reads `-i ''` as in-place editing with the empty string as the script. It then treats the `s|...|` expression as a file name and exits with an error, so on Linux `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated when the key already exists. The script still prints "✅ Updated" because the sed exit status is never checked. Fix: write to a temp file and move it into place, or detect the platform and choose `sed -i` or `sed -i ''`.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved against the current directory, not the script's location.
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` depends on where the script is run from. Run from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), it creates or edits a `.env` in the folder above the repository, and the app never sees the webhook URL. Resolve it from the script's directory instead, for example `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`.

findings.title: The cache timestamp is always formatted with the "en-US" locale.
findings.body: The date ignores the user's locale and time format, so non-US users see dates like MM/DD/YY next to otherwise localised text. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (`i18n.language`) when building the formatter.

findings.title: Failures exit with status 0.
findings.body: `cleanup` always runs `exit 0`, including the rate-limit path and the "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" path. Callers and CI see these failures as success. Pass an exit code to `cleanup` and use a non-zero code on the error paths.

findings.title: Access denial throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as a 500.
findings.body: Passing a credential the user does not own throws a generic `Error`. tRPC turns this into INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN, so it is logged as a server fault. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` instead.
